files_changed.summary: ImportCandidate carries its page; the three rung functions take a page (g1).
Updated the calls for the page argument.
Compose pdfjs text-item + viewport transforms into display boxes (g2).
3 tests: compose, drop blanks, no viewport transform.
Per-candidate page: slug/bbox/reading order and the existing query are session-wide, ranked per page (g1).
Rung-1 scan of the open document (annotations + text per page) and the review (g3).
3 tests: per-page scan, no document, no highlights.

decisions: This imports the OPEN document's own /Highlight annotations, not D-02's separately uploaded note copy, because Lite has no artifact-upload flow. Geometry is therefore correct and no upload is invented; the note-slot upload is recorded as the follow-up.

ImportCandidate carries its page, and the review is session-wide: slug, bbox and reading order are computed per page (that page's existing marks first, then the chosen ones). A page-constant slug/bbox would be wrong on a multi-page import.
pdfjs v6 exposes convertToViewportPoint, not the older convertToViewportRectangle; the adapter builds the rect from its two corners, keeping the min/max the pure parser expects.
The scan reads bytes through the existing shared/lib/pdf seam (OPFS/Storage); it opens the PDF and walks every page, rung 1 only (RULE-19: no OCR, and a real annotation is exact).
The control lives in the rail beside the notes panel; the review is the same 021 component, now per-candidate-page.
